statement_summary: Program meets PCI DSS v4.0.1 and reasonable-security duties; documented
vCISO, PCI technical lead, and PCI compliance owner designated in writing
Annual risk assessment with SP 800-30; targeted risk analyses
Risk acceptance authority by level; guest-safety risks not accepted above Low
Quarterly reporting to the audit committee
Policies reviewed annually; standards reviewed by owners
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions
PCI DSS scope documented and confirmed every 12 months; no SAQ answer without evidence
Card and guest-data vendors under contract, reviewed, with current AOCs and annual status checks
Written PCI DSS responsibility allocation and annual evidence from the franchisor
Independent assessment at least annually
Accurate privacy and security statements; total price in every price display
AI tools approved through the AI governance process before use
Security records kept per the retention schedule
Proportionate sanctions for violations
Unique IDs; no shared accounts without accountability
Least privilege; full card display only for approved roles
MFA for CDE, remote, administrator, email, and cloud access
Access reviews every 6 months; privileged quarterly
Removal on termination date; franchisor systems within 1 business day
Accounts inactive 90 days disabled
Just-in-time administrator rights through the broker; sealed break-glass accounts
Vendor access only when needed, through the broker, with MFA and recording
Authenticator rules; no vendor default passwords
System and interface accounts vaulted, rotated, non-interactive
Server rooms and closets locked with badge access or key log
Immediate reporting of suspected incidents
Runbooks maintained and tested annually, including a card compromise exercise
Incident log records discovery, decision, and determination times
Acquirer notified within 24 hours of suspected card compromise; card brand rules followed
Decision log for every potential breach
Franchisor notified within 24 hours; hotel owner within 48 hours (from 2027)
Evidence preserved; forensics through the insurer and counsel
Ransom only with CEO approval, counsel, insurer, OFAC check, and law enforcement report
Central logging, 12-month retention, daily review of card data system events
Recovery objectives from the BIA; annual tests; quarterly restores
Card numbers found in unexpected places handled as an incident
Lessons learned within 14 days; report within 30 days
Systems and data stores classified and inventoried
Card data only in approved vaults; no sensitive authentication data after authorization
Card numbers masked on display and receipts
Card numbers received through other channels deleted and reported
Encryption in transit and at rest per STD-08
Retention schedule (register 2 years minimum; ID scans 30 days after check-out; recordings 90 days)
Certified destruction of paper and media, including background-check reports
No Restricted or Confidential data in unapproved AI tools
Minimum guest data shared with vendors and the franchisor under contract
Payment device list and weekly inspections
Acknowledgment and training at hire and annually
Only company devices for card data and operations systems
No card numbers by email, chat, text, or paper
Verify identity before giving guest information; watch for social engineering
Report phishing; no self-installed software
Lock screens
Check payment devices each shift and report tampering
Remote access only through approved tools
No sharing of passwords or MFA approvals
Approved AI tools only; no Restricted data in others; review output
Recording announcement on every recorded call; pause before card details
Monitoring notice
